overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the alleged unnoticed quorum deliberation or the sign-in policy, and declined to review a separate April complaint filed on the wrong form.

allegations.summary: Alleged that a quorum of the Commission deliberated outside a noticed meeting, based on statements made in litigation depositions.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complainant did not identify dates of alleged violations and does not clearly allege which members—let alone a quorum—deliberated outside of a noticed meeting, we find that the Commission did not violate the law with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the Commission's sign-in sheet policy for meeting attendees has a chilling effect and excludes citizens from meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Because the sign-in sheet poses no practical barriers to members of the public wishing to attend a meeting, we find that the policy at issue did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A separate April document alleging executive session minutes failures was not filed on the AG complaint form and was declined.
allegations.key_passage: Because this complaint was not properly filed with the Commission, we decline to review its allegations now.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
